name: Legs Up the Wall Pose
intro:
Legs Up the Wall Pose (Viparita Karani) is a deeply restorative yoga posture that promotes relaxation and improves circulation. In this pose, the legs are gently rested against a wall while the upper body remains relaxed on the floor, allowing gravity to support the body. It is known for its calming effect on the nervous system and is often used to relieve stress and fatigue.

This posture helps reduce swelling in the legs and feet, especially after long hours of standing or sitting. It also encourages blood flow back towards the heart, improving overall circulation and promoting a sense of lightness in the body.

Regular practice of Viparita Karani helps calm the mind, reduce anxiety, and improve sleep quality. It is a simple yet highly effective pose suitable for beginners as well as experienced practitioners, especially for relaxation and recovery.

steps.text: Sit sideways next to a wall with one hip touching it.
Gently swing your legs up onto the wall while lying back.
Adjust your hips close to the wall for comfort.
Rest your arms beside your body with palms facing up.
Relax your shoulders and close your eyes.
Breathe slowly and stay in this position for 5-10 minutes.
To release, bend your knees and slowly roll to one side.

benefits: Reduces swelling in legs and feet
Supports recovery after long periods of standing
avoid: You have serious neck or back injuries
You are suffering from glaucoma or eye pressure issues
You have uncontrolled high blood pressure
You feel discomfort while lying flat on your back
You have recent leg or hip injuries
You experience dizziness in inverted positions
You are in late stages of pregnancy (consult a doctor before practice)
